Dialogue_Text: Hey! Are you alright? It looked as if you fainted! Do you need some water? More holy water? Have you experienced something like that before?
Well, it looks like the book wanted to show me a couple of things. These... visions.
That damn book! I knew I shouldn't have touched it! I should have never agreed to any of this! It made me see these... people again...
Oh? What do you mean?

I think my heritage triggered something in this book. It made me see people somewhat connected to my blood and to my story. But it also felt like it was studying me, trying to accept who I am and—it's really hard to describe it.
It clearly corresponds with my heritage. That's all you need to know.
Hmm. I see. It does confirm that this book isn't just big, but that there is more to it.
Do you think it's dangerous?
Yes. I think it is.
I don't know, to be honest.
No, I don't think it is. It just wanted to show me things.
Hah! And what isn't dangerous! Sometimes it feels like Toril is filled with dangerous artifacts from ancient times, cursed gear, or creatures that want to turn you into a snack!
I see. Thank you for your opinion.
Sometimes it does feel like that, yes.

I asked you the question because I would like to keep studying this book, but I also am a responsible woman and I do not want to risk anyone's life. If you're going to tell me that this is going to cause trouble, have fatal consequences—for me or anyone else, even someone on the street, someone I do not know—I won't do it.

There are lines that cannot be crossed, and risks that cannot be taken. I don't want to be that kind of selfish scholar. That is why I always warn those that wish to learn more from my books, but this might be different. This is where we need to make a decision. Together.
Do you think I should study the book or do you think it should be destroyed? It's linked to you, so I'll take your decision seriously.

I think you should study it. The book is linked to me, to my blood. I don't think it's dangerous, and perhaps you'll find something that could benefit you or others. If you do, just—but that knowledge to good use.

Pay me some fee, and you may study it. I helped you take the first step to understanding this thing. I think I deserve a little donation. Or at least some special item, something you wouldn't normally sell. Something that is going to help me on my journey.
I think you should destroy this thing. Nothing good is going to come from this.

I understand, and—yes, of course I will put it to good use. I usually try to be a proud and helpful part of the neighborhood, so if I find out anything useful, I'll help the people of Athkatla keep the city better, or perhaps safer. I think I should also give you a small token of my gratitude.
Ah. Of course, I suppose you're right, and I should have something you'll find useful.
I understand your decision, and you're probably right. I shall destroy the book. I should have something that may help with that.

Let me tell you something more: this was a really interesting adventure. I was quite glad to see you grow better; your skills improved quite a bit, too! And then, you helped me with this book over here, and I'm truly grateful.
No matter if it stays in this holy water or not, I believe it should be gone. No matter what any of you think or believe.
While I do not have much to offer you, know that you're always welcome. And in case you were looking for more souvenirs: you know where to find me!
Good luck on your travels, Hero of Baldur's Gate—and Athkatla!
